pages.text: Start from nothing - literally. Start from $(item)Axiom Schemas$() and the $(item)Empty Set$() (Void Essence, or plenty of Void Lattice). Von Neumann built every number out of empty sets nested inside each other; I am doing the same.
Proofs, $(item)Power Sets$(), $(item)Aleph-Null$(), the $(item)Continuum$() and the $(item)Axiom of Choice$() follow. Choice is what Banach and Tarski needed to double a sphere.

Category theory sits on top: $(item)Category Lattices$(), $(item)Functor Bridges$() and finally the $(item)Topos$() - a universe of mathematics with its own logic. Category theory studies not things, but the arrows between them.
The rules you agree to before you prove anything.$(br2)Made in $(item)Formal Proof Assistant$().
The set with nothing in it - made from the nothing a Void Wraith leaves behind.$(br2)Made in $(item)Formal Proof Assistant$().
The set of all subsets. Always strictly bigger than what you started with.$(br2)Made in $(item)Formal Proof Assistant$().
From every set of sets you may pick one of each. Accept it and spheres can be doubled.$(br2)Made in $(item)Formal Proof Assistant$().
Objects and arrows, and nothing else. All of mathematics fits inside.$(br2)Made in $(item)Formal Proof Assistant$().
A map between categories that keeps every arrow pointing the right way.$(br2)Made in $(item)Formal Proof Assistant$().
